newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Defence chiefs to ease tension in northwest Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: Defence chiefs to ease tension in northwest Cambodia.

text.p: Cambodias two main coalition parties have agreed to pull back forces in a volatile northwest province, where clashes this week left dead on both sides, royalist leader Prince Norodom Ranariddh said on Friday.
The premier was speaking before reports that road access into Battambang, Cambodias second largest city, had been cut for most of the day from the north and southeast because of fighting.

A security official with the U.N. Development Programme said staff of U.N. agencies working in Cambodia had been advised from Friday not to travel between Battambang and Pursat, about 180 km (100 miles) to the southeast on the key highway to Phnom Penh.

He said the order also applied to traffic heading north from Battambang to Sisophon and the border with Thailand, adding that the directive was issued "because there is some problem in Battambang." He did not elaborate.
Unconfirmed reports said the airport at Battambang was closed to air traffic.
Security sources in Battambang said both roads out of Battambang had been blocked at points by military, while access along a key road in the city had also been closed.

Co-Defence Ministers Tea Banh of the Cambodian Peoples Party and Tea Chamrath of the royalist FUNCINPEC party flew to the rice-bowl province of Battambang later on Friday to try and defuse tension, officials said, but the outcome was not known.

"I have suggested to withdraw all of the forces (of the rival parties) back to the previous positions and after that let us resolve the remaining problem," Ranariddh told reporters at a ground-breaking for a new international airport terminal.

FUNCINPEC and CPP troops have clashed this week in Battambangs Moung district, sources from both sides said. The fighting was linked to Khmer Rouge defectors, with some of the former guerrillas siding with the CPP and some with FUNCINPEC.
Human rights workers in Battambang said on Friday they had reports of 16 fatalities in the past three days, including 14 CPP soldiers and two FUNCINPEC soldiers.

Rival premiers Ranariddh and Hun sen, who formed an uneasy coalition after U.N.-run elections in 1993, had been expected to discuss the problems in Battambang and a draft electoral law during a cabinet meeting on Friday.
But Ranariddh said the meeting had been postponed at the request of Hun Sen, who also missed the airport ceremony and travelled instead to open a school in an eastern province.
Conflicting reports have emerged about the fighting from officials of the rival officers contacted in Battambang, with each blaming the other for the clashes.

The clashes in Battambang mark the most serious escalation of tension between the two sides since November clashes between the two sides left several wounded. Ill feelings have continued to simmer despite the intervention of top officials from both sides.
